entities.name: Abune Petros
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abune Petros (c. 1892–1936) was an Ethiopian Orthodox bishop martyred by Italian fascist forces during the occupation of Ethiopia, becoming one of his country's most venerated national and religious heroes. Born in the Wollo region, he was consecrated a bishop of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and served his community during the tumultuous years of Haile Selassie's early reign.

When Italian forces invaded Ethiopia in 1935–1936, Abune Petros refused to collaborate with the occupation and publicly urged Ethiopians to resist. He was arrested by Italian colonial authorities, tried by a military tribunal, and executed by firing squad in Addis Ababa on 29 July 1936. His last words before execution, reportedly urging continued resistance to occupation, transformed him immediately into a symbol of Ethiopian sovereignty and Christian steadfastness.

A statue of Abune Petros stands in central Addis Ababa, and his feast day is observed by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. His martyrdom fused religious faith with national resistance in a way that resonated throughout twentieth-century African Christianity. He represents the broader witness of African Christian leaders who refused accommodation with European colonialism, placing him alongside other anti-colonial martyrs in the history of the global Church.
